item.title: Bangladesh becomes Development Finance Corporation-eligible country
item.description: Bangladesh’s new eligibility status creates an important opportunity for DFC to help address the country’s substantial economic development needs by mobilising private investment, the statement said.
item.content:encoded:
Bangladesh becomes Development Finance Corporation-eligible country Bangladesh’s new eligibility status creates an important opportunity for DFC to help address the country’s substantial economic development needs by mobilising private investment, the statement said. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 23:05 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 23:05 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) today announced that projects in Bangladesh are now eligible for DFC financing, the US Embassy in Dhaka said in a statement on Monday. DFC’s investments in South Asia serve as a stabilising force by supporting energy, critical infrastructure, and technology projects that strengthen our alliances and protect the region’s sovereignty, it added. Bangladesh’s new eligibility status creates an important opportunity for DFC to help address the country’s substantial economic development needs by mobilising private investment, the statement said. Expanded access to DFC financing and risk-mitigation tools will help bridge critical investment gaps and advance projects that might otherwise face financing constraints, it said. These investments will spur economic growth by developing critical infrastructure, creating jobs, expanding access to essential services, and strengthening local businesses, it said. DFC’s support is valuable in helping commercially viable, development-focused projects overcome financing constraints or perceived risks that would otherwise deter private investment, the US Embassy said. “Bangladesh’s eligibility for DFC financing marks an important opportunity to deepen our economic partnership and mobilise private investment that delivers lasting growth. By supporting projects that strengthen critical infrastructure, we can unlock economic opportunity for Bangladesh while advancing U.S. strategic interests,” said Ben Black, DFC CEO. “The United States believes that promoting open economies and reciprocal trade will spur economic growth in Bangladesh, and th Agreement on Reciprocal Trade is our public commitment to supporting Bangladesh through this process. DFC financing can play an important role in making that vision a reality – spurring further prosperity in both of our countries,” said Brent T. Christensen, US Ambassador to Bangladesh. Home to more than half the world’s population and some of its fastest-growing economies, the Indo-Pacific offers significant opportunities for strategic US investment. DFC is committed to helping American businesses expand their presence in the region, mobilizing private capital to advance economic growth rooted in free-market principles and strengthening US  economic partnerships, the statement said. The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to US economic statecraft. DFC mobilises private capital to advance U.S. foreign policyand economic development. (ANI)

item.title: Trump says he "would not mind" Jensen Huang returning as NVIDIA CEO; cautions against ‘insulting’ China ahead of Asia trip
item.description: US President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, suggesting the scandal-hit chipmaker co-founder had "learned a big lesson" while cautioning against ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump says he "would not mind" Jensen Huang returning as NVIDIA CEO; cautions against ‘insulting’ China ahead of Asia trip US President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, suggesting the scandal-hit chipmaker co-founder had "learned a big lesson" while cautioning against taking an aggressive stance that could "insult China" ahead of his upcoming trip to Asia. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 20:57 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 20:57 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/X/@RapidResponse47). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, suggesting the scandal-hit chipmaker co-founder had "learned a big lesson" while cautioning against taking an aggressive stance that could "insult China" ahead of his upcoming trip to Asia. Speaking to reporters before departing for the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, following which he will head to Shenzhen, China, for the APEC summit and a high-stakes trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump weighed in on the mounting Silicon Valley push to bring Huang back just days after he resigned after his extramarital relationship became public. Asked directly whether he wanted to see Huang reinstated at the helm of the USD 4 trillion artificial intelligence giant, Trump signalled openness to the idea even after previously floating Apple CEO Tim Cook as a potential successor. "I would not mind. I would not mind that," Trump said. "I like, you know, I threw out the name of Tim Cook, but I would say that uh Jensen's reinstatement, I think he learned a big lesson, I guess. Maybe one lesson's more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that." Responding to suspicion of Alice Huang being a Chinese spy, Trump said that he is unaware of her true identity while noting that "beautiful women" coming from China are usually considered spies. "I don't know that she's a Chinese spy and I've said that... Usually what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that's a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't," he said. Trump’s remarks stand in sharp contrast to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who argued on Sunday that Nvidia needs a "dramatic shake-up" and an outside chief executive, while demanding answers on whether the company turned a blind eye to chip smuggling to China. When pressed on Bessent’s criticisms and the Commerce Department's handling of export controls, Trump acknowledged competing policy approaches within his administration but stressed the importance of diplomatic restraint before arriving in China. "Well, look, there are two different views. One view is you don't want to insult China. We have a very good relationship with China, and uh you don't want to insult them. And the other view is just go, you know, down and dirty and do what you have to do," Trump said. "Both, you can't say either is wrong or right." Trump noted that strict US export curbs had already prevented Nvidia from selling its most advanced Blackwell processors to Beijing, limiting the company to older hardware. "Jensen, as you know, wanted to sell to China, and the only thing he was able to sell to China were chips that were sort of obsolete. A little bit like our avionics, our aviation equipment. He wasn't allowed to sell the Blackwell or any of that," Trump said. "But no, it's a different approach. Just a different approach. You know, we're heading to China, and I don't think you want to insult China just before you get there." Huang stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who has been accused of spying for China, which triggered an independent board probe and raised questions in Washington over whether restricted US AI chips were diverted to Beijing. The controversy also involved reports of an alleged relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports to Huang. Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, separately reported that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee Despite his exit, major shareholders and tech leaders, including Elon Musk, have rallied behind an open letter calling for his return. Following the push for his reinstatement, Huang has also reportedly discussed the possibility of returning to lead the multi-trillion-dollar chipmaker with close associates, according to the Financial Times. According to the Financial Times, citing multiple people familiar with the matter, Huang has discussed a potential comeback with confidantes even as Nvidia's board conducts an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding his departure. An ally of Huang told the Financial Times that efforts were underway to build a network of influential technology executives to lobby for his return, including seeking support even from the White House. According to the Financial Times, Huang also continues to enjoy considerable support among Nvidia employees, several of whom have publicly called for his return and signed the open letter. The latest developments come as Nvidia's board explores potential successors, with Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas emerging as one of the names under consideration, as per an earlier Financial Times report. Haas, who has led the SoftBank-backed British chipmaker since 2022, previously worked at Nvidia for around seven years more than a decade ago and is understood to maintain professional relationships with Huang and several members of the company's board. However, Nvidia indicated that its succession process remains at an early stage. The company's board said it was "in the process of selecting a search firm" to identify a new chief executive and had not "formally engaged" with any candidates, the Financial Times reported. Huang announced his resignation last week after 33 years at the helm of Nvidia, with Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress currently serving as interim CEO. (ANI)

item.title: India remains top source of international students in US for third consecutive year despite 6% dip: Report
item.description: India remained the largest sender of international students to the United States for the third year in a row during the 2025/26 academic year, even as its total student count fell by six per cent to ...
item.content:encoded:
India remains top source of international students in US for third consecutive year despite 6% dip: Report India remained the largest sender of international students to the United States for the third year in a row during the 2025/26 academic year, even as its total student count fell by six per cent to 339,435, according to the Open Doors 2026 report on International Educational Exchange. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 18:28 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 18:28 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India remained the largest sender of international students to the United States for the third year in a row during the 2025/26 academic year, even as its total student count fell by six per cent to 339,435, according to the Open Doors 2026 report on International Educational Exchange. The report showed that while graduate enrollments from India dropped by 34 per cent to 116,609 and undergraduate numbers slipped by one per cent to 39,711, participation in Optional Practical Training (OPT) rose by 27 per cent to 182,201 students. China stayed in second place, though its student count declined by four per cent to 254,458. Overall, US colleges and universities hosted 1,146,163 international students from over 200 countries in 2025/26, representing a three per cent decrease from the previous year and accounting for six per cent of the total US higher education population. New international student enrollments declined by 18 per cent to 228,123. "The 2026 Open Doors data reaffirms the enduring importance of international education to the United States," said Jason Czyz, President and CEO of the Institute of International Education. "By investing in global engagement, US colleges and universities enable American and international students to build connections that advance long-term research and economic collaboration. These experiences strengthen US institutions and build relationships that extend beyond students' time on campus," Czyz noted. The report mentioned that international students contributed nearly USD 56 billion to the American economy in 2025. Across all nationalities, graduate students formed the largest group at 423,078 despite a 13 per cent drop, while OPT participation expanded by 14 per cent to 335,785. Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields attracted 57 per cent of all international students, led by math and computer science at 286,168 and engineering at 214,193. Meanwhile, nine of the top 25 sending countries- Bangladesh, Canada, Colombia, Ghana, Italy, Nepal, Pakistan, Peru, and Vietnam- recorded all-time highs. The report also tracked outbound mobility for the 2024/25 academic year, showing that 313,824 US students studied abroad for academic credit, up five per cent. Europe hosted 64 per cent of these students, with Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom ranking as the top destinations. "The 2026 Open Doors findings offer an important lens into how US study abroad is evolving in response to changing academic, economic, and global conditions," Mirka Martel, PhD, Head of Research, Evaluation and Learning at the Institute of International Education, said. "International experiences help American students develop cross-cultural competencies and technical skills that prepare them for professional opportunities when they return to the United States," Martel added. Looking ahead, a preliminary Fall 2026 Snapshot of more than 800 US institutions pointed to a nine per cent drop in total international enrollments for the 2026/27 academic year, with 91 per cent of surveyed colleges prioritizing STEM student recruitment. (ANI)

item.title: Four members of Baloch family remain missing after reported detentions in Winder and Khuzdar, six others return home
item.description: Four members of the same family remain missing following alleged detentions by Pakistani forces in Winder and Khuzdar, while six other men who had reportedly been subjected to enforced disappearances ...
item.content:encoded:
Four members of Baloch family remain missing after reported detentions in Winder and Khuzdar, six others return home Four members of the same family remain missing following alleged detentions by Pakistani forces in Winder and Khuzdar, while six other men who had reportedly been subjected to enforced disappearances in separate incidents across Balochistan have returned home, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP). ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 18:26 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 18:26 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Four members of the same family remain missing following alleged detentions by Pakistani forces in Winder and Khuzdar, while six other men who had reportedly been subjected to enforced disappearances in separate incidents across Balochistan have returned home, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP). Citing local sources, TBP reported that Frontier Corps (FC) and Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel raided two houses in Winder on October 12. The four family members reportedly remain missing following the alleged detentions. Meanwhile, local sources in Tump, in Kech district, reported overnight raids on several houses by Pakistani forces and members of an armed group they described as a state-backed "death squad". According to the report, those involved allegedly took cash, gold jewellery, vehicles and other valuables from the houses during the raids. The allegations have raised further concerns over the safety of civilians and incidents of intimidation and looting in the region. In a separate development, six men who had reportedly been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces have returned home, TBP reported. Among those released are three residents of Gujjar in the Mashkay area of Awaran district, who had reportedly been missing since February 2. Their return marks a development for their families, who had been awaiting information about their whereabouts. Meanwhile, the protest camp organised by the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) outside the Quetta Press Club continued for its 6,420th day on Sunday. Visitors to the camp expressed solidarity with families of missing persons and called for an end to enforced disappearances in Balochistan. VBMP Chairman Nasrullah Baloch described enforced disappearances as unconstitutional, unlawful and a serious violation of human rights, demanding the recovery of all missing persons. "If any person is accused of an offence, they should be presented before a magistrate within 24 hours and the legal requirements should be fulfilled," he said. He further held the government responsible for ending enforced disappearances, safeguarding citizens' constitutional and legal rights, and ensuring justice for affected families. (ANI)
